propositions: The rebar-debug skill lacks an initial setup directive to isolate work in a fresh worktree.
Without worktree isolation, Phase 2 code changes (RED tests and fixes) can land on a stale branch in the primary checkout, violating project contributor rules.
A directive instructing `git worktree add` based on `origin/main` must be placed at the start of skill execution to enforce isolation before any debugging or reproduction work begins.
The skill's two-phase debugging protocol remains semantically unchanged; only the execution preamble is augmented with the concrete worktree mechanism.
